role_name: Enterprise Sales Manager – Agentic AI Solutions
role_description: Owns full-cycle enterprise pursuit and closure of Agentic AI solutions. Bengaluru, work-from-office.
paper_title: Candidate Screening Form – Enterprise Sales Manager, Agentic AI Solutions
paper_notes: Questions are identical to the Account Manager - Enterprise Sales screening form, as requested, transcribed from Account_Manager_Candidate_Screening_Form (3).docx with the additional AI-products question at position 12. All questions are free-text; marks are not used.

questions.question_text: Where are you based these days?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational. Note whether the location is compatible with daily attendance at the Bengaluru office, and flag any relocation requirement.

questions.question_text: This role is based in Bengaluru and is a work-from-office (WFO) position, with client travel as needed. Are you comfortable with this?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Screening gate covering two things: daily office attendance and willingness to travel to clients. Look for a clear yes to both. Flag any constraint on travel, since the role requires it.

questions.question_text: What is your educational background? Please mention your degree and specialization.
questions.instructions: This role requires an engineering degree (CS, IT, ECE or related).
questions.evaluation_criteria: Stated requirement for this role: an engineering degree in CS, IT, ECE or a related discipline. Record the degree and specialisation, and flag clearly if it is absent so the hiring manager can decide whether to waive it.

questions.question_text: How many years of enterprise B2B sales experience do you have, and how many of those were spent selling Cybersecurity, AI Security, Cloud or IAM solutions?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Two figures matter, and the second matters more: total enterprise B2B years, and years specifically in Cybersecurity, AI Security, Cloud or IAM. Check both against the products and deals described in questions 6, 7 and 10.

questions.question_text: How would you define your current role, and how do you see yourself fitting into this Account Manager position at Valamm.AI?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Two parts, both needed: an accurate description of what they do today, and a considered link to this role. Look for an understanding that account management here means retention, renewal and expansion of existing enterprise relationships, not only new-logo hunting.

questions.question_text: Which Cybersecurity, AI Security, Cloud or IAM products have you sold, and to which Indian enterprises or industries?
questions.instructions: For example: SIEM, endpoint, IAM / PAM, cloud security, AWS / Azure / GCP; BFSI, manufacturing, IT/ITeS.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for named product categories actually sold and named industries or accounts in the Indian market. Depth in one or two relevant segments beats a list covering everything. Credit answers that make the claim checkable.

questions.question_text: Pick one product you have sold. In simple words, explain how it works technically and what problem it solves for the customer.
questions.instructions: Please answer in plain, simple language and avoid jargon or buzzwords.
questions.evaluation_criteria: The technical-comprehension question. A good answer explains the mechanism in plain language - what the product actually does, where it sits in the customer's environment - and ties it to a concrete business problem. Deduct for a recited marketing pitch, for jargon substituting for understanding, or for an explanation that could not survive a question from a customer's engineer.

questions.question_text: Have you sold to Global (non-Indian) enterprise accounts? Please describe briefly.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Nice to have. Credit named markets or accounts, time-zone coverage, and comfort with international enterprise buying processes. An honest no with relevant adjacent experience is acceptable.

questions.question_text: Describe how you defined an ICP (ideal customer profile) and built a target-account list for it. What outreach did you run against that list, and what were the results?
questions.instructions: For example: ABM, LinkedIn / social selling, email, partner-led or event-led outreach.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests method rather than activity. Look for explicit ICP criteria (industry, size, tech stack, trigger), how the list was built and prioritised, the channels and cadence run against it, and measurable results - meetings, pipeline, conversion. Deduct for a list handed to them by someone else, or outreach described with no outcome.

questions.question_text: Which CXO-level buyers (CEO, CISO, CTO, CIO) have you sold to directly? Walk us through one deal from first contact to closure – stakeholders, commercials, negotiation.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Highest-signal question on this form. Look for direct CXO access (particularly CISO for this product set) and a coherent end-to-end deal narrative: how first contact was made, the buying committee, the commercial structure, how negotiation and procurement were handled, and who actually decided. Deduct where CXO contact was only ever via a manager, or the story lacks commercials and negotiation detail.

questions.question_text: What were your annual / quarterly revenue targets over the last two years, and how did you perform against them? What was your largest deal size?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for real figures across two years - quota, attainment, and largest single deal - and internal consistency with the deals described elsewhere. Credit candidates who know their own numbers without prompting. Treat unquantified claims of over-achievement as weak.

questions.question_text: Have you sold AI products or software into enterprises? Which industries do you know best?
questions.instructions: For example: BFSI, Manufacturing, Healthcare, Retail, IT, Education.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for concrete AI or software products sold, the buyer personas reached, and named industries with genuine depth rather than a list of every vertical. Honesty about where their depth actually lies is worth more than unevidenced breadth.

questions.question_text: Tell me about an account where you drove a renewal, upsell or cross-sell. What did you do?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Directly tests the core of this role. Look for a named account, the state it was in, what the candidate personally did to secure the renewal or expansion, how value was demonstrated, which stakeholders were involved, and the commercial outcome. Credit expansion earned off demonstrated value rather than a discount.

questions.question_text: Tell me about a recent deal you lost, and why.
questions.instructions: For example: lost to a competitor, pricing challenge, budget freeze, or something else.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests candour and diagnosis. Look for a real, recent loss owned without deflection, an honest root cause, and a specific change made afterwards. Deduct for blaming product, pricing or the customer entirely, or for claiming no recent losses.

questions.question_text: What is your current notice period, current CTC and expected CTC (fixed + variable)?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational, for offer planning. Look for the notice period and both CTC figures with a fixed/variable split. Do not judge the candidate on the amounts; note only whether the expectation sits inside the approved band.

questions.question_text: Please share your convenient days and preferred time slots so that we will try to schedule the calls accordingly.
questions.instructions: For example: Tuesday to Thursday, 10:00 AM - 1:00 PM IST. More than one option helps us find a time that works for everyone.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Scheduling information. Look for at least one day with a time slot; several options make the panel easier to arrange. Note any constraint the candidate mentions (notice period, current-employer hours, time zone) and pass it to whoever books the calls.
